name: Tracy's Blue Phoenix
reason: Possessive extraction artifact; the mentions refer to the Blue Phoenix, the localized name of Tracy's (Mo Yuxin's) Qing Luan bloodline beast.
description: The Blue Phoenix is the bloodline phantom of Tracy, one of the Sect's Chosen, corresponding to the Mythical Beast Qing Luan of the source novel.

name: Burning the Life-Essence
reason: A forbidden sacrifice technique named descriptively for the Western fantasy register; no exact source term surfaced in the evidence, though the lifespan-burning act occurs in the source Peak Competition arc.
description: A desperate technique in which a warrior burns their life essence, sacrificing lifespan for power. Zane stopped Tracy from resorting to it during the competition arc (Ep 285).

name: Storage Ring Zane
reason: Tokenization artifact of 'Storage Ring' followed by 'Zane'; the mentions belong to the Storage Ring, the localization of the source's Sumeru Ring spatial device.
description: Spatial storage equipment carried by warriors; Zane's storage ring appears throughout the early episodes.

name: Thousand Blossoms
reason: Short form of 'Sword of a Thousand Blossoms', Evan's light and nimble sword style in Eps 320-322, which localizes the source's 'Vibrant Falling Petals Sword' (ch ~308).
description: Evan's signature light, nimble sword style, the pride of the Skyreach Sect's top-ranked fighter; Zane studied it for weaknesses during their arena duel.

name: Gale
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Gale' was chosen as a short, forceful name echoing the strength of the source's Huo Gang, a grassroots-born top sect disciple recruited by the Third Prince.
description: A top-ranked disciple of the Skyreach Sect (source: Huo Gang of the Azure Cloud Sect's Heaven's Fury Peak). Born into poverty, his allegiance to the Third Prince was bought with cultivation resources, yet his pride as a Skyreach disciple drove him to defend Zane's reputation when onlookers mocked him (Ep 340).

name: Otto
issues: Likely a merged entity: 'Otto' in Ep 80 is a Misty Peak pledge ranked sixteenth beaten in the peak matches, while 'Otto' in Ep 349 is a guard of Connor at the primary Inner-Core Realm; these appear to be two different minor characters sharing one localized name.
reason: A minor character name localized to the short Western name 'Otto'; no confident single source counterpart, and the two uses appear to cover different source minor characters.
description: A minor male name used twice: a Misty Peak pledge defeated by Eagle Peak in the peak matches (Ep 80), and later one of Connor's strongest guards, outmatched by Sir Kenneth (Ep 349).

name: Mystical Pace
reason: A movement technique name coined for the Western fantasy register; the source scene (Luo Zheng's spatial step technique on the Azure Clouds Road) exists, but no exact source term surfaced in the evidence.
description: A movement technique tied to Spatial Law perception, first identified by Toby Dillon when watching Zane navigate the Cloud Road (Ep 360); Zane later uses it in combat as a shimmering, blink-like step (Ep 714).

name: River-Winds
reason: Short form of 'Scythe of the River-Winds', the cooperative formation weapon of Eps 368-370, localizing the source's 'Wind of Kan' attack of the Twelve Earthly Branches Formation.
description: A cooperative formation weapon powered by the Formation of the Twelve Signs, requiring all thirteen Cloud Hall disciples including Lennon.

name: Ice Phoenix Tia
reason: Concatenation artifact of 'Ice Phoenix' followed by 'Tia'; the mentions refer to the Ice Phoenix projection that Tia conjures from her sky-blue gem.
description: The icy phoenix projection summoned by Tia via her sky-blue gem; unlike most warriors' fleeting illusions, hers stood out, though it remained an illusion compared to later true summons (Eps 394, 818).

name: Secluded Cultivation
reason: Generic cultivation-genre common noun (closed-door training), capitalized stylistically; not a distinct named entity.

name: Snow Drake
reason: Source term 'Snow Flood Dragon' was localized as 'Snow Drake' for the Western fantasy setting; the Ep 409 scene (a five-hundred-foot scorched beast at a warrior's feet) matches the source's fifty-zhang Snow Flood Dragon beneath a flame-wreathed man.
description: A ferocious draconic beast of the Flood Dragon line native to lands of ice and snow; a massive five-hundred-foot specimen lies slain and scorched at a warrior's feet in Ep 409.

name: Spear of Annihilation
reason: The source spear technique 'Revolving Spear Demon God Twist' (Zhuo Bufan's killing move, ch ~399) was renamed 'Spear of Annihilation' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: Frank's devastating signature spear technique; surviving it is treated as a mark of exceptional strength (Eps 412-413).

name: House Novak
reason: A noble house name localized to 'House Novak' in keeping with the show's Legacy House naming conventions; no confident source clan match surfaced in the evidence.
description: A Tier-Two noble force of the Imperial City region, ranked well below the Seven Great Houses (Ep 427); by Ep 653 its line has been reduced to a single surviving princess.

name: Thunderoak
reason: Short form of 'Amethyst Thunderoak', the rare lightning-attuned treasure wood on Twilight Peak that Zane seeks in Eps 428-430.
description: A five-thousand-year-old lightning-attributed treasure material sought by Zane and hunted by warriors on Twilight Peak.

name: Wraithgold
reason: The source's 'dark golden ropes' used by slavers to bind captives (ch ~418-420) were given the evocative material name 'Wraithgold' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A dark-gold binding material shot from mechanisms as ropes; seven or eight Wraithgold ropes wrapped and tightened around Zane before he severed one (Ep 429).

name: Hell-Crow
reason: The source beast 'Sky Goblin Crow', an evasive aerial attacker Luo Zheng baits in the early trial arc, was renamed 'Hell-Crow' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A scavenger crow-beast that harries Zane from the air; he exploits its scavenger nature by baiting it with a free meal (Ep 45).

name: Cobalt Fibers
reason: A weapon name coined in the show's cobalt/blue color scheme for a Trial-arc opponent's thread weapon; no exact source term surfaced in the evidence.
description: A storm of whirling blue thread-like weapons wielded by Joe during the trial arc, forming a defensive barrier that made charging him suicidal (Eps 45-46).

name: Indigo Blade
reason: The source's 'Zi Qing Sword' (purple-azure treasure sword, a high-grade profound weapon) was localized as 'Indigo Blade'; the master sheet explicitly confirms this over earlier literal renderings like 'Purple-Blue Sword'.
description: Julian Croft's prized saber, a top-tier blade on par with elite weapons of its grade. Zane claims and examines it closely after the confrontation in Eps 56-61.

name: Matriarch's Core
reason: The source's 'Blade Insect Queen's crystal core' was localized as the 'Matriarch's Core' of the Razorwing Queen; the exchange values match exactly (1,000 points, equivalent to 2,000 Crystal Cubes).
description: The crystal core harvested from the Razorwing Queen; Zane exchanged it for one thousand Points, worth two thousand Crystal Cubes (Ep 97).

name: Ice Spikes
reason: Generic capitalized attack phrase with no supporting context; not a distinct named entity.

name: Infernal Peak Zane
reason: Tokenization artifact of 'Infernal Peak' followed by 'Zane'; the mentions belong to Infernal Peak, the mountain training ground of Eps 87-99.
description: A mountain location and training ground visited by Zane in Eps 87-99.

name: Tenth Tribulation Introducing Pill
reason: The source's 'Ten Direction Calamity Guide Pill', a tribulation-attracting pill offered as a top competition prize, was localized as the 'Tenth Tribulation Introducing Pill'.
description: An extraordinarily precious pill that can attract a heavenly tribulation for its user, though not infallibly. It was the true prize of the competition in Ep 1080, worth more than any weapon offered, and warriors offered first-grade divine tools in exchange for it.

name: Sixth Small Heavenly Tribulation
reason: The source's ordinal 'minor heavenly tribulation' milestones of the Divine Sea stage were localized as 'Small Heavenly Tribulations'; this entry is the sixth in the sequence.
description: The sixth of the ordinal lightning tribulations a Divine Sea-stage warrior must weather as they advance; Zane feels his sixth gathering as his strength grows (Eps 1039, 1103).

name: Tenth Small Heavenly Tribulation
reason: Source term 'tenth minor heavenly tribulation' was localized as 'Tenth Small Heavenly Tribulation', keeping the ordinal tribulation terminology consistent.
description: The legendary tenth and final minor heavenly tribulation, which only the most monstrous geniuses ever trigger; spectators pray Zane will face it (Eps 1030-1032), and Jasper later kicks off his own (Ep 1103).

name: Thirteen Palaces’
reason: Possessive surface form of 'Thirteen Palaces', the Upper Realm coalition of palaces kept under its source name.
description: The thirteen great palaces of the Upper Realm arc whose geniuses compete in inheritances and trials.

name: Nether God
reason: Likely a localization of the source's 'Dark God' (as in the Thundergale Dark God Sword), renamed 'Nether God' for the Western fantasy register; the match rests on the elemental sword imagery and is low confidence.
description: A spectral deity whose shadow flickers among the storm of elements Zane unleashes in the late Divine Sea arcs (Eps 1125-1220).

name: Supreme Lord Leroy
reason: A Celestial Venerable-tier figure of the source's late arcs given the localized title 'Supreme Lord' and the US-origin name 'Leroy'; no confident source-name match surfaced in the evidence.
description: One of the Supreme Lords, the Celestial Venerable-tier powers who loom over the late Upper Realm arcs (Eps 1055-1175).

name: Saint Sky Armor
reason: The source's 'Vast Sky Treasure Armor', one of the few supreme divine artifacts able to block world-shattering power, was localized as 'Saint Sky Armor'.
description: A supreme defensive artifact of the late arcs, counted among the few treasures in the universe capable of withstanding shattering-class power (Eps 1169-1184).

name: Supreme Lord Armond
reason: A Celestial Venerable-tier figure of the source's late arcs given the localized title 'Supreme Lord' and the US-origin name 'Armond'; no confident source-name match surfaced in the evidence.
description: A Supreme Lord commanding devastating flames; even his hottest fire only slowed the burning of the Star of Golden Sand, and a single object survived his tempering (Eps 1183-1184).

name: Radiant Sand
reason: A rare material name coined for the Western fantasy register in the Star of Golden Sand arc; no exact source term surfaced in the evidence.
description: An extraordinarily rare luminous sand; the amount gathered in Eps 1172-1173 is said to exceed anything ever assembled in the universe.

name: Palace of Heavenly Punishment
reason: The source's 'Punishment Seizing Palace' within the Night Clan's Hall of Punishment was localized as the 'Palace of Heavenly Punishment'.
description: A towering palace that once stood like a beacon; more than twenty elders descended on it in a single morning without its doors opening once (Ep 1174), mirroring the source's gathering before the Punishment Seizing Palace.

name: Crowns of Destiny
reason: Plural surface form of 'Crown of Destiny', the source's fate-granting crown artifact (also rendered 'Heaven's Mandate Crown' in source translation).
description: Coveted crown artifacts tied to the Mandate of Heaven, a fatal temptation said to let a Realm Lord ascend to Celestial Venerable.

name: Supreme Lord Ranell
reason: A Celestial Venerable-tier figure of the source's late arcs given the localized title 'Supreme Lord' and the name 'Ranell'; no confident source-name match or gender evidence surfaced.
description: A Supreme Lord hostile to the Demi-Immortal Race's involvement in the contest over Zane, sneering at Marcello's claims (Eps 1184-1189).

name: Marcello
reason: The character's source name was fully localized to the US/European-origin name 'Marcello' for a Supreme Lord of the Demi-Immortal Race; no confident pinyin match surfaced in the evidence.
description: A Supreme Lord of the Demi-Immortal Race who calmly faces the other Supreme Lords' hostility, declaring that Zane passed his race's test, earned the golden celestial rank, and counts as one of their people (Ep 1185).

name: Illusory Space
reason: Source term 'Illusory Space' was carried over unchanged, fitting the adaptation's fantasy register.
description: A projection-based combat space of the Upper Realm arcs where warriors' real fighting strength is tested without shortcuts; Layla watches Zane's feats inside it in disbelief (Eps 1091-1204).

name: Low Grade-One Divine-Class
reason: The source's divine-weapon grading ('first-grade divine weapon') was localized into the show's Divine-Class tier terminology, with 'Low' marking the lower band of grade one.
description: A weapon-quality tier in the late-arc divine grading system; Zane's bare fingers carving grooves into a Low Grade-One Divine-Class weapon demonstrates his monstrous physical strength (Ep 1210).

name: Death Chain
reason: The source's 'Life Ending Shackle', which binds the user to their opponent, was renamed 'Death Chain' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A high-risk binding technique that locks the user to an opponent so neither can escape, suicidal against a stronger foe. Saul explains its uses to Zane (Eps 992-993), and Zane later seals his victory by locking it onto Sloane (Ep 1238).
